name: NPWA World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Traced back to the fed's own 1993 founding (Bash, its first champion), the belt changed hands six times across 1997 alone -- Amoral to Locutus to Col. Buddy Lee Jarrett to 'Superstar' Steve Sampson to 'Blackheart' Brian Masters, a November vacancy, and finally 'Hollywood Heartthrob' Dave Diamond's win in a 14-man Pinfall Royale at the fed's own year-end Xmas Gory '97 -- along the way surviving a stolen-belt cliffhanger left unresolved on a satellite cut-off.

name: NPWA North American Championship
epitaph: Created for 1997 exactly as the fed's own 1996 FAQ had promised ('a third singles belt on the way early in '97'), first won by 'Sadistic' Steve Stone in a 15-man King of the Hill gauntlet at the fed's own Valentine's Day Massacre '97, and defended in turn by 'Breakfast' Bobby Toast and Mustafa before the Cougar carried it into 1998.

name: NPWA World Television Championship
epitaph: Crowned by a 16-man tournament in late 1996, the title changed hands six times across 1997 -- the Southern Rocker to Jurisprudence to the Mighty Boss to 'Bad Boy' Mark Bagwell to 'Blackheart' Brian Masters to the Silent Striker to Dark Justice, who carried it into 1998's own Death Row Match.

name: NPWA World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: A lineage reaching back to the NWC era, the belts changed hands four times across 1997 alone -- the New Cadavre Connection to the Muslim Massacre (their challengers flying Vegas to London on the Concorde mid-show to turn) to the Lords of the Ring to the Asian Triad -- before a further change and a forfeiture carried the title to Drama by year's end.

name: NPWA Millennium Championship
epitaph: Created for the NPWA's own Millennium Division sometime before the held record's June-August 1998 gap, first held by "Untouchable" Randy Gant before "Superstar" Steve Sampson took it in a chaotic Coal Miner's Glove three-way at Mayhem, 29 Sep 1998.

name: NPWA North American Tag Team Championship
epitaph: A second NPWA tag championship, first held by The Cult (Doctor Death & Father Armageddon, with Locutus wrestling in Armageddon's stead) before changing hands twice in three weeks -- to Assault and Battery at the fed's 5th Anniversary Special, then to the Masters of Disaster at Hell On Earth.

name: NPWA Cruiserweight Championship of the World
epitaph: Held throughout the 1998 run by an undefeated Atticus "The Jester" Payne, criticized on-air for rarely putting the belt on the line.
